lines.text: Why do airplane windows have a tiny hole?
It's not a mistake. It's called a bleed hole.
Your window is really three panes, not one.
At cruising altitude, the cabin air is pressurized, so it pushes hard against the window.
The hole lets that pressure into the gap, so the outer pane takes the load.
The middle pane is the backup, in case the outer one is ever compromised.
The hole also lets moisture escape, so your window doesn't fog up.
So that little dot in your photos? It's a safety feature.
